<explanation>
Based on the project’s file tree and README content, here’s how you should approach drawing a system design diagram that accurately captures the architecture of the PIKE-RAG system:

1. Project Type & Purpose:
   • PIKE-RAG is a specialized retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework. Its purpose is to enhance LLM outputs by integrating domain-specific knowledge extraction, document parsing, and multi-step reasoning.
   • The system is organized into several modules that handle document loading, knowledge extraction, knowledge retrieval, and prompt-based reasoning. It is used to power pipelines that are configurable for various tasks (e.g., multi-hop question answering).

2. Analyzing the File Structure:
   • Top-level directories like “pikerag”, “data_process”, “examples”, “docs”, and “docker_files” indicate a modular design.
   • The “pikerag” directory contains key modules:
     - document_loaders and document_transformers: handling data ingestion and formatting.
     - knowledge_retrievers: which includes several retrieval strategies (BM25, Chroma, etc.) and query parsing utilities.
     - llm_client: interfaces with different LLM providers (Azure, HuggingFace).
     - prompts: containing all the logic for different prompting techniques (chunking, decomposition, tagging).
     - workflows: orchestrating pipeline steps for QA, evaluation, and other processing.
   • The “data_process” directory provides scripts for parsing raw data and preparing benchmark datasets.
   • “examples” contains sample configurations and pipelines (e.g., for HotpotQA, MuSiQue) to demonstrate how the system is to be used.
   • The presence of configuration files (YAML) and docker files indicates support for both dynamic pipeline configuration and containerized deployment.

3. Key Architectural Elements to Capture in Your Diagram:
   a. Main Components:
      - Data Input & Preprocessing:
        ▫ Data Ingestion and Processing modules (e.g., scripts in data_process) which pre-format datasets.
        ▫ Document Loading and Parsing (found in pikerag/document_loaders).
      - Knowledge Extraction and Transformation:
        ▫ Document Transformers (e.g., filters, splitters, taggers) under pikerag/document_transformers.
        ▫ Various specialized prompt modules (chunking, decomposition, tagging) that help in preparing the knowledge base.
      - Knowledge Retrieval:
        ▫ Multiple knowledge retrieval components (BM25, Chroma, hybrid methods) under pikerag/knowledge_retrievers.
      - LLM Integration:
        ▫ LLM Client modules (in pikerag/llm_client) that abstract calls to external LLM services.
      - Workflow Orchestration:
        ▫ Workflows (found in pikerag/workflows) that coordinate the overall end-to-end pipelines (QA, evaluation, tagging).
      - Supporting Components:
        ▫ Utility functions, configuration loader, logging etc., spread across utilities and scripts.
        ▫ Deployment and containerization support reflected in docker_files.
   b. Relationships & Interactions:
      - Data flows from ingestion (document loaders) → transformation (document transformers) → knowledge storage.
      - Retrieval components then query processed and stored knowledge to prepare prompts.
      - The LLM client integrates with these components via the workflows to generate responses.
      - Configuration files (YAML) guide the behavior of each module; this allows for plugging in alternate strategies (e.g., different retrieval backends or prompt templates).
   c. Architectural Patterns:
      - Modular design: encapsulating different responsibilities (data handling, transformation, retrieval, reasoning) in separate directories.
      - Pipeline orchestration: series of discrete steps chain together to form a full end-to-end response generation framework.
      - Extensibility: use of configuration files and multiple implementations (plugins) for document processing and retrieval.
   d. Relevant Technologies & Tools:
      - Python as the primary language.
      - YAML for configuration.
      - Docker for deployment.
      - Third-party APIs/integrations for LLMs (Azure OpenAI, HuggingFace).
      - Likely use of libraries for natural language processing and retrieval (e.g., BM25, Chroma).

4. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:
   • Since this is a specialized framework (rather than a generic full-stack app), emphasize the modular pipeline – display each core module as a distinct component.
   • Illustrate how data flows through preprocessing, knowledge extraction, retrieval, and reasoning by drawing directional arrows between components.
   • Include separate sections for static configuration (YAML files), examples that enable different pipelines, and deployment artifacts (docker files).
   • Optionally, you can also show external systems (e.g., external LLM API endpoints, benchmark datasets) that interact with the PIKE-RAG system.

5. Instructions for the Principal Software Engineer on Diagram Elements:
   - Clearly label each component:
     ▫ For example, label “Document Ingestion”, “Knowledge Extraction & Transformation”, “Knowledge Retrieval”, “LLM Client”, and “Workflow Orchestration”.
   - Use arrows to denote data flow or dependencies:
     ▫ Arrow from “Document Loaders” to “Document Transformers” then to “Knowledge Retriever”.
     ▫ Arrows from “Workflows” to “LLM Client” to represent where LLM responses are generated.
   - Use color coding and distinct shapes:
     ▫ You might use one color/shape for processing components (e.g., document parsing and transformation), another for orchestration (workflow modules), and a third for external service integration (LLM client).
   - Ensure the diagram is detailed:
     ▫ For each pipeline stage, include submodules if relevant (such as different types of document transformers or knowledge retrievers) so that the diagram gives a full picture of the system’s extensibility.
   - Emphasize modularity:
     ▫ Include a note that each module is configurable via YAML settings and can be swapped for different implementations (as shown in the examples directory).

6. Final Diagram Composition:
   - Start with an “Input Layer” that encompasses data ingestion (from raw data to parsed documents).
   - Next, a “Processing Layer” that hosts knowledge extraction components (document transformers, prompt generation, filtering, splitting).
   - Follow it with a “Retrieval Layer” that retrieves relevant knowledge using various underlying strategies (BM25, Chroma).
   - Then, an “LLM Integration Layer” where the LLM client receives the prepared prompts to generate answers.
   - Finally, a “Workflow/Orchestration” component that ties everything together and coordinates the entire pipeline.
   - Surrounding the core with auxiliary components (deployment configurations, example pipelines, and diagnostics/logging).

By following these instructions and tailoring the diagram to capture the modular, configurable, and pipeline-driven nature of PIKE-RAG, you will provide a detailed and accurate high-level overview of the system’s design. This diagram will be valuable both for understanding the system’s flow and for identifying key points for future enhancement or debugging.
</explanation>
